subject: science
title: Launch and diagnostic: biological scale and measurement

standards.legacy_label: Science and engineering practice foundation - this unit claims no Michigan performance expectation.

essential_question: What counts as biological evidence, and how do the molecules of life make structure and function inseparable?
learning_objectives: Observe the anchoring phenomenon, surface initial thinking about biological scale and measurement without penalty, and pose a testable question.
Explain biological scale and measurement using evidence, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
Apply biological scale and measurement to a task the learner has not seen before, showing the reasoning that produced the result.
Check and revise the work on biological scale and measurement against the stated success criteria and name the next step.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about biological scale and measurement.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process, not a bare answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and identifies one specific next step.
Any quantity the learner reports is one the learner measured, computed, or cited to a named published source.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
pencil, keyboard, or other accessible response tool
printed or on-screen text, data table, or model for this lesson

lesson_flow.title: Retrieval and phenomenon check
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with the unit phenomenon - Two apple slices, one left plain and one coated in lemon juice, brown at very different rates on the same counter. - or a short retrieval prompt on biological scale and measurement. Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, or question before any instruction. Record the prediction; it is not graded.

lesson_flow.title: Model or mini-lesson
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Develop biological scale and measurement from the phenomenon: pose the testable question, build or use a model, and show how evidence constrains the explanation. Name the success criteria and demonstrate how to check the work. Phase focus: Launch and diagnostic.

lesson_flow.title: Guided practice
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Work two supported examples on biological scale and measurement, asking after each move: what evidence or reasoning supports that step? Fade the prompting on the second example and have the learner narrate the check.

lesson_flow.title: Independent application
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: The learner completes a new application of biological scale and measurement independently and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.

lesson_flow.title: Exit evidence and next step
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: In one concise response, the learner shows or explains the most important idea about biological scale and measurement, then names one check that would catch an error or a weak claim in their own work.

student_activity: The learner completes a new application of biological scale and measurement independently and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about biological scale and measurement, then name one check that would catch an error or a weak claim.
scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target: accuracy, quality of evidence and reasoning, and evidence of checking or revision. Accept any valid approach that meets the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error. Do not award credit for a numerical result that the learner did not measure, compute, or cite to a named source.
extension_activity: Apply biological scale and measurement under a new constraint, compare two approaches or two sources, or teach the idea with an original example. Extension never means completing another learner's graded work.

hazards.description: Desk-based work only; no chemicals, heat, electricity, or tools are used in this lesson.
hazards.mitigation: Materials are notebook, writing tool, and printed or on-screen text. Any hands-on extension defers to the unit investigation's safety review.

sensitivity: Content is academic; no personal, family, health, or location disclosure is requested.
stop_conditions: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.

Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.

hazards.description: 3% hydrogen peroxide irritates eyes and can bleach fabric and skin on contact.

hazards.description: Catalase and peroxide foam vigorously and release oxygen.

hazards.description: Slicing produce with a kitchen knife risks cuts.
hazards.mitigation: An adult does all cutting, or the learner uses pre-cut produce; no knife work is required by the lesson.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): Isopropyl alcohol is flammable, its vapour is heavier than air and pools at bench level, and it is harmful if swallowed or splashed in eyes.
MITIGATION: An adult sweeps the room for every ignition source before the bottle is opened, pours no more than 60 mL, and returns the bottle to a closed cupboard at once. Eye protection on; nothing is tasted. See the safe order.
HAZARD (physical): Glass containers can break and cut.
MITIGATION: Use plastic or unbreakable cups only.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. An adult sweeps the room before the bottle is opened: hob and oven off, heater off, no candle, pilot light, toaster, charger, or battery anywhere.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Put on eye protection. Mash the fruit and add the soap-and-salt water and filter it, all with no alcohol yet in the room.
  SAFE ORDER 3. An adult brings in the cold isopropyl, pours no more than 60 mL into the learner's cup, caps the bottle, and returns it to a closed cupboard at once.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Observe and spool the DNA with the cup on a tray, at least three metres from any appliance or outlet.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Dispose of the alcohol mixture before anything electrical is switched on at that surface again.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if alcohol contacts the eyes and rinse for 15 minutes.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Cutting cubes to size uses a knife.
MITIGATION: An adult does all cutting, or the learner uses clay shaped by hand with no cutting tool.
HAZARD (physical): Microscope lamps get warm and slides have sharp edges.
MITIGATION: Handle slides by their edges, let the lamp cool before storage, and treat the microscope step as optional.
HAZARD (physical): Broken slide glass cuts whoever empties the bin.
MITIGATION: An adult sweeps fragments with stiff card, wraps them in thick paper and tape, and bins them separately. Never by hand, never loose, never with a vacuum cleaner.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Clear and wipe the work surface before anything is set out.
  SAFE ORDER 2. An adult does every cut; the learner receives pre-cut cubes or shapes clay by hand with no cutting tool.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Measure and record every cube before any liquid is added.
  SAFE ORDER 4. If the microscope route runs, an adult mounts the slide and the learner handles it by its edges only.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Switch the lamp off and let it cool before anything is packed away.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if a slide chips or breaks and let an adult clear it as described.
  STOP: Stop if anyone reaches for a knife; all cutting is done by an adult.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Clay goes back into its container and potato cubes into the compost or bin; pour coloured water down the drain and rinse the containers. An adult clears any broken slide by sweeping the fragments with stiff card, wrapping them in thick paper and tape, and binning them separately - never by hand, never loose, never with a vacuum cleaner.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Do the whole unit with no microscope and no cutting: use published, openly licensed onion-root-tip micrographs to count cells in each mitotic phase, and model surface-area-to-volume with hand-rolled clay cubes measured with a ruler.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Cutting cubes to size uses a knife.
MITIGATION: An adult does all cutting, or the learner uses clay shaped by hand with no cutting tool.
HAZARD (physical): Microscope lamps get warm and slides have sharp edges.
MITIGATION: Handle slides by their edges, let the lamp cool before storage, and treat the microscope step as optional.
HAZARD (physical): Broken slide glass cuts whoever empties the bin.
MITIGATION: An adult sweeps fragments with stiff card, wraps them in thick paper and tape, and bins them separately. Never by hand, never loose, never with a vacuum cleaner.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Clear and wipe the work surface before anything is set out.
  SAFE ORDER 2. An adult does every cut; the learner receives pre-cut cubes or shapes clay by hand with no cutting tool.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Measure and record every cube before any liquid is added.
  SAFE ORDER 4. If the microscope route runs, an adult mounts the slide and the learner handles it by its edges only.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Switch the lamp off and let it cool before anything is packed away.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if a slide chips or breaks and let an adult clear it as described.
  STOP: Stop if anyone reaches for a knife; all cutting is done by an adult.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Clay goes back into its container and potato cubes into the compost or bin; pour coloured water down the drain and rinse the containers. An adult clears any broken slide by sweeping the fragments with stiff card, wrapping them in thick paper and tape, and binning them separately - never by hand, never loose, never with a vacuum cleaner.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Do the whole unit with no microscope and no cutting: use published, openly licensed onion-root-tip micrographs to count cells in each mitotic phase, and model surface-area-to-volume with hand-rolled clay cubes measured with a ruler.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): Baking soda solution irritates eyes.
MITIGATION: Wear eye protection and rinse any splash with water.
HAZARD (physical): A lamp close to a water container gets hot and mixes electricity with water.
MITIGATION: Use an LED lamp only - never incandescent or halogen, which crack a cup and can ignite paper at this distance. Keep it at least 30 cm away, never above the water, and plug it in away from any spill zone; an adult positions the lamp.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water scalds, and hot tap water kills the yeast anyway.
MITIGATION: An adult mixes the yeast water and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 40 degrees Celsius. Temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
HAZARD (physical): A syringe with a needle, or a blocked tip under vacuum, injures or sprays.
MITIGATION: Use a needleless blunt-tip syringe only. No needle of any kind is used in this course.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. An adult positions the LED lamp first, at least 30 cm from any container and never above it, with the cord away from the spill zone.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Decomposing material grows mould, and mould aerosol is far more dangerous to an asthmatic than to someone with hay fever.
MITIGATION: Anyone with asthma, an immune condition, or a mould or spore allergy uses the alternative and opens nothing. Containers stay outdoors, labelled, covered LOOSELY so gas escapes - never sealed. Gloves on; open outdoors only.
HAZARD (physical): Mould-colonised matter on a food scale contaminates everything weighed afterwards.
MITIGATION: Weigh in a disposable tray placed on the scale; the sample never touches the scale surface. The containers, trays, and gloves belong to this investigation only and are binned at the end. None of it returns to kitchen or food use.
HAZARD (privacy): Recording an outdoor location can disclose where the family lives.
MITIGATION: Record habitat type and general conditions only. Never record an address, GPS coordinate, or identifiable landmark.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Label two containers and a set of disposable trays for this investigation only; nothing here has ever been used for food and nothing returns to food use.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Confirm nobody in the household has asthma, an immune condition, or a mould or spore allergy. If anyone does, run the alternative and open nothing.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Put on gloves before touching soil or scraps, and set the containers up outdoors or in a garage, out of reach of pets and young children.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Cover LOOSELY with cloth or punctured foil so gas escapes; never seal a container.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Weigh by placing the sample in a disposable tray on the scale - the sample never touches the scale surface.
  SAFE ORDER 6. Open containers outdoors only, at arm's length, with the face turned away, and wash hands thoroughly before coming indoors.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop and switch to the alternative if anyone in the household has asthma, an immune condition, or a mould or spore allergy.
  STOP: Stop if a container has been sealed rather than loosely covered; let an adult open it outdoors, away from faces.
  STOP: Do not open a container that smells strongly or looks heavily colonised; bag it unopened and bin it outdoors.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Bag the containers and contents unopened and put them in the OUTDOOR waste bin. Do not compost indoors and do not empty anything into a food-waste caddy. The container is never sealed while it is decomposing - it is bagged only at the very end, for the outdoor bin. The containers, trays, and gloves are binned with them and never return to kitchen or food use.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Skip the decomposition setup: build the energy budget and carbon flow entirely from a published, openly licensed ecosystem dataset and a species list, using arithmetic and a drawn web. Paper only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Decomposing material grows mould, and mould aerosol is far more dangerous to an asthmatic than to someone with hay fever.
MITIGATION: Anyone with asthma, an immune condition, or a mould or spore allergy uses the alternative and opens nothing. Containers stay outdoors, labelled, covered LOOSELY so gas escapes - never sealed. Gloves on; open outdoors only.
HAZARD (physical): Mould-colonised matter on a food scale contaminates everything weighed afterwards.
MITIGATION: Weigh in a disposable tray placed on the scale; the sample never touches the scale surface. The containers, trays, and gloves belong to this investigation only and are binned at the end. None of it returns to kitchen or food use.
HAZARD (privacy): Recording an outdoor location can disclose where the family lives.
MITIGATION: Record habitat type and general conditions only. Never record an address, GPS coordinate, or identifiable landmark.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Label two containers and a set of disposable trays for this investigation only; nothing here has ever been used for food and nothing returns to food use.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Confirm nobody in the household has asthma, an immune condition, or a mould or spore allergy. If anyone does, run the alternative and open nothing.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Put on gloves before touching soil or scraps, and set the containers up outdoors or in a garage, out of reach of pets and young children.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Cover LOOSELY with cloth or punctured foil so gas escapes; never seal a container.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Weigh by placing the sample in a disposable tray on the scale - the sample never touches the scale surface.
  SAFE ORDER 6. Open containers outdoors only, at arm's length, with the face turned away, and wash hands thoroughly before coming indoors.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop and switch to the alternative if anyone in the household has asthma, an immune condition, or a mould or spore allergy.
  STOP: Stop if a container has been sealed rather than loosely covered; let an adult open it outdoors, away from faces.
  STOP: Do not open a container that smells strongly or looks heavily colonised; bag it unopened and bin it outdoors.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Bag the containers and contents unopened and put them in the OUTDOOR waste bin. Do not compost indoors and do not empty anything into a food-waste caddy. The container is never sealed while it is decomposing - it is bagged only at the very end, for the outdoor bin. The containers, trays, and gloves are binned with them and never return to kitchen or food use.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Skip the decomposition setup: build the energy budget and carbon flow entirely from a published, openly licensed ecosystem dataset and a species list, using arithmetic and a drawn web. Paper only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (privacy): Online dataset searching can expose the learner to tracking or to accounts.
MITIGATION: An adult supplies the dataset file or the exact source; no account creation, sign-in, or purchase is required.
HAZARD (physical): Small counters are a choking hazard around young children, and dried beans used as counters are no longer food - raw kidney beans in particular are toxic if eaten.
MITIGATION: Keep counters away from younger siblings, count them back into a labelled container at the end, and never return beans used as counters to food storage or eat them.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. An adult supplies the dataset file or the exact source before any browsing begins.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Count the beans into their container in a shallow tray, with young children out of the room.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Run each sampling trial and record it before mixing again.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Count every bean back into the container and confirm the total before leaving the work area.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if a website asks for an account, payment, or personal information.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Beans and counters go back into a labelled container stored out of reach of young children. Beans used as counters are never eaten and never returned to food storage. Dataset files stay on the adult's device; nothing is uploaded.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Run a mark-and-recapture sampling model with two colours of dried beans in a bag to estimate an unknown population, then compare the estimate to the true count. Kitchen materials and arithmetic only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.

  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (privacy): Online dataset searching can expose the learner to tracking or to accounts.
MITIGATION: An adult supplies the dataset file or the exact source; no account creation, sign-in, or purchase is required.
HAZARD (physical): Small counters are a choking hazard around young children, and dried beans used as counters are no longer food - raw kidney beans in particular are toxic if eaten.
MITIGATION: Keep counters away from younger siblings, count them back into a labelled container at the end, and never return beans used as counters to food storage or eat them.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. An adult supplies the dataset file or the exact source before any browsing begins.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Count the beans into their container in a shallow tray, with young children out of the room.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Run each sampling trial and record it before mixing again.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Count every bean back into the container and confirm the total before leaving the work area.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if a website asks for an account, payment, or personal information.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Beans and counters go back into a labelled container stored out of reach of young children. Beans used as counters are never eaten and never returned to food storage. Dataset files stay on the adult's device; nothing is uploaded.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Run a mark-and-recapture sampling model with two colours of dried beans in a bag to estimate an unknown population, then compare the estimate to the true count. Kitchen materials and arithmetic only.

hazards.description: Small counters and dried beans are a choking hazard around young children and are no longer food.
hazards.mitigation: Keep counters away from younger siblings, count them back into a labelled container, and never return them to food storage or eat them.

hazards.description: Family trait or pedigree work can expose genetic and health information about relatives who never consented.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Timed grabbing games can knock over nearby objects.
MITIGATION: Clear the work surface first and keep the play area away from edges and breakables.
HAZARD (emotional): Extinction and habitat loss can be genuinely upsetting.
MITIGATION: Frame the unit around designed responses and documented recoveries; the learner may pause or choose a different case at any point.
SUPERVISION: you may work on this independently. Tell an adult before you start anyway.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Clear the whole work surface and move screens and breakables out of reach before any timed round.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Agree the rules and the timer length, then run one practice round untimed.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Run each timed generation and record the counts immediately, before the next round starts.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Count every counter back into its container at the end.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Pause if the extinction content becomes distressing and resume with a recovery case study.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
